steps.caption: The big screen on the right is the master output: what your audience sees.
Below it, a preview of each of the four decks: A, B, BG and PV.
A and B are the main decks. The crossfader mixes between them.
BG is the background deck: it is drawn behind A and B.
Its level starts at zero. Drag its fader up and BG appears behind deck A.
Deck A draws only part of the frame, so BG fills in around it.
PV is the preview deck. Try things out here: the audience never sees it.
On the left is the Perform view: rows of knobs, grouped into pages. This is the A/B page.
The BG/PV page holds the BG and PV decks.
MIXER holds the deck levels, the master FX chain, transitions and the clock.
Back to A/B. Perform is one of three views; the other two are Edit ({ch:edit}) and Library ({ch:library}).
Every deck has two rows. The top row, SRC, is its source: the shader that draws the picture.
The row below is the deck's FX chain. Here it is switched off.
BYPASS turns the whole chain on or off. Click it, and the picture runs through the effects.
More on FX in {ch:fx}. Sources first.
Click the source name to browse sources and presets for that deck.
Click a source in the list and it loads straight into the deck.
Each click swaps the deck's source. Watch deck A's preview and the output.
And back to Kifs.
Save stores the deck's source and all its settings as a preset.
The gear opens the Edit view with every parameter of the row ({ch:edit}).
The FX row below is the deck's effect chain ({ch:fx}).
Every row has four knobs, mapped to that row's most useful parameters.
Drag up or right to turn a knob up...
...and down or left to turn it down.
Hold Shift while dragging for fine control. Double-click a knob to type a value.
Under the output is the crossfader. It blends deck A into deck B.
The same crossfader is the first knob of the Transitions row on the MIXER page.
Turn it and the crossfader under the output follows.
The other knobs shape the transition: how deck A becomes deck B.
Every deck has an FX chain with three slots. The master has one too.
The picture flows through the slots from left to right: slot 1, then 2, then 3.
So order matters. Here Kaleidoscope folds the image, then Polar Tunnel wraps the result into a tunnel.
Swap them, and the tunnel is folded instead. Same effects, a very different picture.
Drag a slot onto another to reorder the chain.
The power button switches one slot off without removing it.
Each slot's knob is that effect's Metaknob: one knob that drives its main parameters.
The Super Knob turns the Metaknobs of every linked slot at once.
A slot joins in when the Super Knob passes its current value, so nothing jumps.
The link button above a slot adds it to the Super Knob or takes it out. Click to unlink Polar Tunnel.
Now the Super Knob moves only the linked slots. Polar Tunnel stays put.
Click again to link it back.
The link beside the Super Knob links or unlinks all slots at once.
The master FX chain on the MIXER page works the same way. It runs after the crossfader, on the final mix.
The gear on a row opens the Edit view.
Edit lists every parameter of the deck's source, not only the four on the knobs.
K1 to K4 mark the parameters that sit on the row's four knobs.
VAL sets a parameter's value. LFO and the other columns add modulation.
Click a parameter to see and edit its properties.
The FX tab shows the deck's chain: wet/dry, the Super Knob and every slot's parameters.
These checkboxes are another way to choose which slots follow the Super Knob.
The tabs on the far left jump to the other decks and to the mixer.
The Library view fills the screen with your sources, effects and presets.
Tabs switch between sources, FX, transitions, queues and macros.
Search finds items by name, tag or folder.
Preferences, under General, has the theme.
There are two: dark, and this light one for bright rooms.
